chunks: My father (RA) said: `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Fuddal, from `Ali ibn `Uqbah, from his father, who said: I heard Abu `Abd Allah (AS) say:

Leave your matter for Allah, and do not leave it for the people. Whatever is for Allah belongs to Allah alone, and whatever is for the people will not ascend to Allah. Do not argue with the people about your religion, for verily arguing is an illness of the heart.
Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He pleases.
Will you then force men till they become believers?

Leave the people, for verily the people take their knowledge from each other, while you have your knowledge from the messenger of Allah (SA). Verily, I have heard my father, Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) say that `Verily, when Allah, the Mighty and High, writes that a servant should enter a matter, then he is quicker than a bird to its nest.”

key_terms.لِدِينِكُمْ: For your religion (in context of argumentation)
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For Allah (dedication of affairs to God)
key_terms.لِلْقَلْبِ: For the heart (location of the spiritual state)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of arguing with people about religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid underscores the Shia principle of sincerity (ikhlas) by contrasting divine acceptance with the ephemeral nature of human approval, while cautioning that religious disputatiousness corrupts the heart's spiritual state. It reinforces the theological distinction between human effort and divine guidance, noting that true adherents are drawn to the Imamate with the natural urgency of birds returning to their nests, a metaphor for the innate recognition (fitrah) of the faithful.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 13. My father (RA) said: `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn al-Fuddal, on the authority of `Ali ibn `Uqbah, on the authority of his father saying that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Leave your matter for Allah, and do not leave it for the people. Whatever is for Allah belongs to Allah alone, and whatever is for the people will not ascend to Allah Do not argue with the people about your religion, for verily arguing is an illness of the heart.
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, said to His Prophet (SA) Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He pleases.
He has also said: Will you then force men till they become believers?

Leave the people, for verily the people take their knowledge from each other, while you have your knowledge from the messenger of Allah (SA). Verily, I have heard my father, Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) say that `Verily, when Allah, the Mighty and High, writes that a servant should enter a matter, then he is quicker than a bird to its nest.”
